instruction: Use the terminal to launch GIMP for editing "cola.png", remove the right 15% of the image, and save the result as "cropped.png".

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires cropping right 15% of cola.png (1233x1280). Expected result: 1048x1280. Verified: 1233 * 0.85 = 1048 pixels width (rounded).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the core requirement: checking if 15% was removed from the right side of the image by validating final dimensions (1048x1280)
Expected values are mathematically correct: 1233 * 0.85 = 1048 pixels (rounded), height unchanged at 1280
Getter logic is sound: downloads file from VM using env.controller.get_file(), uses PIL to extract dimensions, returns tuple (width, height)
Metric logic is appropriate: compares actual vs expected dimensions with 2-pixel tolerance, which is reasonable for image cropping operations
Data flow is correct: getter extracts dimensions -> metric compares with expected -> returns 1.0 for match or 0.0 for mismatch
Error handling is robust: handles missing files (None return) and image open failures gracefully
Dimension check is sufficient to verify task completion: only removing right 15% yields 1048x1280 result, other crop operations would produce different dimensions
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: No postconfig to ensure file is saved, but acceptable since the instruction explicitly requires saving and file existence check inherently verifies the save step
